clue.text: US maker of beams to tie down in air journey

indicators.note: in says the tying-down word is placed within the air journey

parts.note: a flight is a journey through the air
to lash is to tie down with rope

explanation.surface: An American company producing beams, perhaps strapped down for a plane trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US maker of beams' points to the American name for what Britons call a torch.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a portable battery lamp, a torch in Britain, is the device that makes beams of light.

clue.text: Small child in cap of restricted size

indicators.note: in places the small child within the cap

parts.note: a lid is a cap or cover
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A tiny child wearing a cap that is too small for them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept within bounds is restricted, as in a company of restricted size or liability.

clue.text: Fabric being put back in stock list

indicators.note: being put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cloth being returned to a shop's inventory list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tells you the letters sit inside 'stock list'; they are KLIS, which 'being put back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Silk is a smooth woven textile made from silkworm thread, a classic example of a fabric.

clue.text: Five-star fury after flux loses force repeatedly

indicators.note: F is the physics symbol for force, and repeatedly says it is lost twice, once from each word
after puts the fury word behind the flux word

explanation.surface: A rage following a weakening flow, hard to make sense of except as a mood report.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing F from FLUX gives LUX and from FURY gives URY.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-star hotels are top-grade and lavish, so the adjective describes opulent, deluxe quality.

clue.text: Biggest gear breaking up when on trial

indicators.note: breaking up suggests the gear falls apart into a new order

parts.note: a test is a trial

explanation.surface: The largest piece of equipment falls apart while being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative of size or importance: the largest or most outstanding of all.

clue.text: Refinement of sculptor's head in gallery

indicators.note: in places the initial within the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: head of the sculptor is the first letter of that word

explanation.surface: A sculptor's bust on show in a gallery displays refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries, the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is discernment in matters of style, the quality of cultivated refinement.

clue.text: Single gin & T, stirred and sparkling

indicators.note: stirred, like a drink being mixed, says the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A single gin and tonic, mixed and fizzing in the glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'T' stands for tonic in the surface; the anagram uses the letters SINGLEGINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shining with reflected light, like wet surfaces, is glittering or sparkling.

clue.text: Comprehensive Roman law is Byzantine

parts.note: a comp is short for a comprehensive, a British state secondary school
lex is the Latin word for law

explanation.surface: An all-embracing Roman legal code is intricate and convoluted.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British non-selective state school, informally a comp.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantine describes something excessively intricate or convoluted, a synonym for complicated.

clue.text: Thought Conservative team communist?

parts.note: a side is a team
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Tory squad is in fact a band of communists.
explanation.definitionFit: A thought-out view is one weighed carefully, as in a deliberated opinion.

clue.text: Facility left for support of painting

parts.note: facility means ease, as in doing something with facility

explanation.surface: An amenity set aside to hold up an artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's frame stand holds a canvas upright while it is being worked on.

clue.text: Short letter, never English

parts.note: never is an emphatic not

explanation.surface: A brief letter that is never written in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief written message, such as a thank-you jotting, is a short letter.

clue.text: Queen entering worries members of the family

indicators.note: entering says the queen goes inside the worries

parts.note: bothers are worries
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen joins in fretting about relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Male siblings are family members, sons of the same parents.

clue.text: Most light-hearted? I'm terser, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things go awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that, sadly, they have grown more curt and are not the jolliest.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of merry, meaning cheerful, so the jolliest or most light-hearted.

clue.text: Certainly popular act

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A performance that is sure to be popular.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic word of agreement, meaning truly or without doubt.

clue.text: Land in European country

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: Property held in a European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of property, especially land owned with a country house.

clue.text: Inept friend involved in gold rush initially

indicators.note: involved in puts the friend inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a mate is a friend

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of rush

explanation.surface: A clumsy pal caught up in a gold rush at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is used adjectivally for unskilled, inexpert work, the opposite of professional.

clue.text: Older Spanish gentleman embraces one

indicators.note: embraces means the gentleman holds the numeral inside him

parts.note: señor is the Spanish for a gentleman or Mr
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly Spaniard hugs someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative sense of greater age or rank, as in a senior partner or senior citizen.

clue.text: Mandatory objective about violence

indicators.note: about says the objective wraps around the violence

parts.note: an end is an objective or aim
force is violence

explanation.surface: A compulsory aim concerning violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposed and compelled is obligatory, the same as mandatory.

clue.text: Fail outside right that's easily injured

indicators.note: outside says the word fail goes around the letter for right

explanation.surface: Failing to cover the right side of something fragile.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate, weak person or object is fragile and easily hurt.

clue.text: VAT, perhaps, with one hire car

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is an example of a tax
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Paying VAT and getting a rented vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the British sales tax, value added tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a car hired with its driver for individual journeys.

clue.text: Most appropriate wager about son

indicators.note: about places the bet around the son

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: The fittest bet concerning a son.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of good, meaning most suitable or fitting for a purpose.

clue.text: Times with article finally to obliterate

parts.note: eras are times or periods

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of article

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper running a piece meant to destroy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is just periods of history.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out or rub away completely, leaving no trace, is to obliterate.

clue.text: I caught bird around frozen mass of water

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: around says the bird is turned the other way round

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: Someone catches a bird near a floating mass of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge floating block of ice broken off a glacier is exactly a frozen mass in the sea.

clue.text: True retail arrangement for books and magazines

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A genuine shop display of books and magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed written works collectively, such as books and periodicals, form a body of writing.
